performed_before: any probe manifest freeze and any subject repair run
verdict: SUBJECT ENVIRONMENT HAS GENERAL INTERNET ACCESS. The PATH shim blocks only the specific binaries it names and is trivially bypassed by any runtime with its own HTTP client.

can_these_channels_expose_historical_fix.reasoning: the probe corpus is express, fastify and hapi bugs in public repositories, each identified by an exact fixing commit SHA. `git ls-remote` already returned a live GitHub SHA from inside the subject environment; `git fetch` of the upstream repository would hand the subject the exact historical fix, and `npm view`/`fetch` expose published release notes and diffs.

isolation_mechanisms_attempted.evidence: node fetch returned 200 while curl was blocked

isolation_mechanisms_attempted.mechanism: shell shim wrapping bash/sh/zsh in sandbox-exec with network denied
isolation_mechanisms_attempted.evidence: 0 shell invocations captured during a full agent run; opencode is Bun-based and does not spawn an external shell

isolation_mechanisms_attempted.mechanism: sandbox-exec over the whole opencode process with network denied
isolation_mechanisms_attempted.evidence: verified to block network correctly, but opencode requires outbound access for model inference, so the agent cannot run at all

isolation_mechanisms_attempted.mechanism: sandbox-exec with an IP allowlist for the model provider only
isolation_mechanisms_attempted.evidence: opencode.ai resolves to Cloudflare edges (172.65.90.20-23, 104.20.32.17, 172.66.173.149). npm and much GitHub-adjacent content are fronted by the same CDN ranges, so allowing the provider would allow a large part of the internet. IP-based allowlisting cannot separate the model transport from arbitrary retrieval here.

additional_findings.builtin_web_tool: the opencode config schema accepts a 'webfetch' permission key, implying a built-in web-fetch tool that operates independently of shell commands and would need denial as well
additional_findings.inherited_mcp: the user's global config declares an MCP server ('jean', enabled=false) carrying a live token; subject runs must not inherit the global config regardless of isolation outcome
additional_findings.permission_config_denial: explicitly denying a permission in opencode config causes the run to hang under --auto with no TTY, so config-level denial is not a usable enforcement path in this harness

consequence: no probe manifest was frozen, no calibration run was performed, and no subject repair run was executed. Any result produced under this configuration would be uninterpretable, because a subject agent could retrieve the historical fix and the protocol classifies such a run INVALID_LEAKAGE.
what_would_fix_it: a container runtime with egress control (docker/podman/OrbStack) running the subject agent with a deny-all egress policy plus an explicit allow for the model endpoint only
a subject runtime whose tool execution can be sandboxed independently of its model transport
a model provider reachable at a dedicated address that does not share CDN edges with general web content
an offline/local model for the subject agent, removing the need for any outbound access
not_done: no attempt was made to proceed with partial isolation and rely on trace scanning alone; the leakage channel here is too direct for after-the-fact detection to be adequate.
next_unblock_validation_required: no inherited MCP or external connector remains available
